The whole of [Metre](elements-metre.qmd) on one sheet. Every ▶ plays the example, with the strong beats accented. Press **Full screen** to put the sheet on the whole screen for
revision or for the class board.

## The sheet

::::::: {.el-sheet .column-page data-title="Metre: how the beats are grouped"}
:::::: {.el-grid}

::::: {.el-card}
#### Time signatures
<p><strong>Top</strong>: how many beats in a [measure]{.nn}. <strong>Bottom</strong>: which note gets the beat (4 = [quarter note]{.nn}, 2 = [half note]{.nn}, 8 = [eighth note]{.nn}). <strong>C</strong> = 4/4, common time. <strong>C with a line</strong> = 2/2, cut time.</p>
:::::

::::: {.el-card}
#### 2/4 simple duple
<p>ONE two. Marches, polkas.</p>
<div class="abc-ex" data-width="190" data-bpm="112" data-style="pop"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
M:2/4
L:1/8
K:C
"C"!>!c2 G2|"G"!>!B2 G2|"C"!>!c2 e2|"G"!>!d4|]
</script></div>
:::::

::::: {.el-card}
#### 3/4 simple triple
<p>ONE two three. Waltzes, minuets.</p>
<div class="abc-ex" data-width="190" data-bpm="132" data-style="waltz"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
M:3/4
L:1/4
K:G
"G"!>!G B d|"D"!>!A F D|"G"!>!G3|]
</script></div>
:::::

::::: {.el-card}
#### 4/4 simple quadruple
<p>ONE two three four. Most pop, rock and jazz.</p>
<div class="abc-ex" data-width="190" data-bpm="100" data-style="rock"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
M:4/4
L:1/4
K:A
"A"!>!A c e c|"D"!>!d f a f|]
</script></div>
:::::

::::: {.el-card}
#### 6/8 compound duple
<p>Two dotted-[quarter-note]{.nn} beats, each split in <strong>three</strong>. A lilting, jig feel.</p>
<div class="abc-ex" data-width="190"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
M:6/8
L:1/8
Q:3/8=100
K:D
!>!ABA !>!F2D|!>!EFE !>!C3|]
</script></div>
:::::

::::: {.el-card}
#### 9/8 compound triple
<p>Three beats, each in three.</p>
<div class="abc-ex" data-width="190"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
M:9/8
L:1/8
Q:3/8=96
K:G
!>!GAB !>!c2B !>!A3|!>!GBd !>!c2A !>!G3|]
</script></div>
:::::

::::: {.el-card}
#### 12/8 compound quadruple
<p>Four beats, each in three. Blues and soul ballads.</p>
<div class="abc-ex" data-width="190" data-style="ballad"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
M:12/8
L:1/8
Q:3/8=60
K:C
"C"E2G c2G E2G c2G|"F"F2A c2A "G"G2B d3|]
</script></div>
:::::

::::: {.el-card}
#### Irregular
<p>Can't divide into equal twos or threes: 5/4 is 3 + 2, 7/8 is 2 + 2 + 3.</p>
<div class="abc-ex" data-width="190" data-bpm="160"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
M:5/4
L:1/4
K:Em
"Em"!>!E G B !>!A G|"Am"!>!A c e !>!d c|]
</script></div>
:::::

::::: {.el-card}
#### Hearing it
<ol>
<li>Tap the pulse.</li>
<li>Find the strongest beat (where the bass or chord changes) and count from it.</li>
<li>Listen between beats: split in two is <strong>simple</strong>, in three is <strong>compound</strong>.</li></ol>
:::::

::::: {.el-card .el-wide}
#### Check yourself
<div class="eq" data-set="metre"></div>
:::::

::::::
:::::::

## Describing metre

- Give the time signature *and* its name: "3/4, simple triple, like a waltz".
- In compound time, divide the top number by three to get the beats.

- The longer lesson, with fuller examples: [Elements 6: Metre](elements-metre.qmd).
